title: A Date's calendar day, in a named zone

blocks.text: A `java.util.Date` is a moment: milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00Z, with no calendar day and no wall clock of its own. Turning it into a `LocalDate`, or a `LocalDateTime` into a `Date`, therefore needs a zone.

items: `dayOf(Date date, ZoneId zone)`: the calendar day `date` falls on in `zone`.
`toDate(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone)`: the `Date` for the moment that `local` names on `zone`'s clock.

blocks.text: Use **the zone passed in**, and only that one: the server's default zone must make no difference, and it is never changed.
(A `Date` is shown here by the instant it holds.)

cases.says: In UTC, a Date's day is its UTC day and a local date-time is that UTC moment.
23:30 UTC on March 15 is March 16 in Tokyo and still March 15 in New York.
10:00 on March 15 in New York is the Date for 14:00 UTC.
On a server whose default zone is UTC+14, both conversions still use the zone passed in, and the default zone is still UTC+14 afterwards.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: The same Date late in the UTC evening can be a different LocalDate east and west of UTC.
ZoneId.systemDefault() makes a conversion depend on the server, so the zone is passed explicitly.
A Date is a UTC-based moment, so turning it into a LocalDate or a LocalDateTime into a Date needs a time zone.
